question.problem:
Find $\text{E}[\frac{{e}^{X-Y}}{1-X}],$ given that random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}{e}^{y},\, & 0\le x\le 1,\,x\le y\le 1,, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are continuous random variables, and $f(x,y)$ is their joint probability density function. If $r:{R}^{2}\to R$ is a function of two variables, then the rule of the lazy statistician states that

$$
\text{E}[r(X,Y)]={∬}_{{R}^{2}}r(x,y)\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
r(x,y)=\frac{{e}^{x-y}}{1-x}.
$$

Now, let's sketch the region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,x\le y\le 1\},$ where $f(x,y)$ is nonzero.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14154787/assets/bc44d4c99cf60148685a99b5c3b5ea2e732ea4b9939aefe5ba465d46e92c5ea8.png)

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[\frac{{e}^{X-Y}}{1-X}] & ={∬}_{{R}^{2}}\frac{{e}^{x-y}}{1-x}\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{{e}^{x-y}}{1-x}\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x}^{1}\frac{{e}^{x-y}}{1-x}\cdot {e}^{y}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{{e}^{x}}{1-x}{\int }_{x}^{1}\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{{e}^{x}}{1-x}\cdot [y]_{y=x}^{y=1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{{e}^{x}}{1-x}(1-x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =[{e}^{x}]_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =e-1.\end{aligned}
$$
